claim: Generalised Lomb-Scargle recovers the period of an irregularly sampled rider to better than 1% of the period, where the slotted autocorrelation argmax cannot name a period at all.
author: claude, session 2026-08-05
reason: passed on solve(), rejected broken(), rejected null()
residence_reason: Passed, and NOT graduated into field/. Wiring it into route() would make the loop start naming periods, and field_claim_loop.py currently reports period_s=None on purpose after two handles were measured and refused. Whether the loop should name a period at all is a design decision about what the router is allowed to conclude, which is the author's call and not a scoring outcome. It sits ACTIVE so every review re-scores it.
why: Recovers Poisson-sampled rider periods to 0.15-0.66% of the true period at n=200, sigma 0.3, and its own broken() (a rider at 2.7x the claimed period) and null() (white values, same clocks) are both rejected by the period checks.
would_change_verdict: A rider class it cannot see. The frequency grid runs from 1/span up to a pseudo-Nyquist set by the MEDIAN sampling gap, so a burst-sampled record with a long tail of gaps has an fmax set by the dense part and will miss nothing, but a record with a few very tight pairs gets an fmax far above what the bulk supports and will alias. Untested. Also: TOL_FRAC 0.01 is a tolerance nobody derived -- it is what the estimator happened to achieve, which makes the check partly circular. Deriving a tolerance from the sampling and the noise level would flip it either way honestly.

checks.check: peak power clears the noise ceiling
checks.detail: weakest median peak power 0.842 against ceiling 0.25

checks.check: white series stay under the ceiling
checks.detail: 95th percentile of max power on noise = 0.156

claim: The loop conserves information, as shown by the fact that its energy is non-negative.
author: the bench itself, as a self-test
reason: every check passed broken(). An assertion no input can make fail is not evidence -- it is the defect this bench exists to catch.
residence_reason: ACTIVE deliberately, and it must stay that way. It is not a failure being kept for provenance -- it is the bench's self-test. If it ever returns anything other than REJECTED_UNFALSIFIABLE, the gate has broken and every SURVIVES verdict in this archive is suspect.
why: All three checks are true for every possible input -- a variance is never negative, a set is never empty, a norm is never below zero -- so they pass broken() as readily as solve().
would_change_verdict: Nothing that keeps it the same candidate. It would need different checks, and different checks make it a different submission. This is the one entry here whose rejection is not provisional.
